stories.headline: US Adds 115,000 Jobs in April, Nearly Double the 62K Forecast; Unemployment Holds at 4.3%

key_facts.fact: Total nonfarm payroll employment edged up by 115,000 in April 2026, with the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.3 percent
key_facts.excerpt: Total nonfarm payroll employment edged up by 115,000 in April, and the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.3 percent, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today.

key_facts.fact: April hiring far exceeded the FactSet consensus forecast of about 62,000-65,000 jobs
key_facts.excerpt: The US economy added 115K jobs in April 2026, following an upwardly revised 185K increase in March, and way above market forecasts of 62K.

key_facts.fact: Job gains concentrated in health care (+37,000), transportation and warehousing (+30,000), and retail trade (+22,000); federal government employment fell by 9,000
key_facts.excerpt: Health care and transportation/warehousing companies led job growth in April, adding 37,000 and 30,000 jobs, respectively. Federal employment fell by 9,000.

key_facts.fact: February payrolls were revised down 23,000 to a loss of 156,000; March was revised up 7,000 to a gain of 185,000
key_facts.excerpt: The change in total nonfarm payroll employment for February was revised down by 23K to -156K and the change for March was revised up by 7K to 185K.

key_facts.fact: Average hourly earnings rose 0.2% in April to $37.41; over the year, wages have grown 3.6%
key_facts.excerpt: In April, average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls rose by 6 cents, or 0.2 percent, to $37.41. Over the year, average hourly earnings have increased by 3.6 percent.

key_facts.fact: Employers added an average of 48,000 jobs per month from February to April, down from 61,000 over the prior three months
key_facts.excerpt: From February to April, employers added an average of 48,000 jobs per month, down slightly from 61,000 over the previous three months.

stories.headline: Ukraine Drone Strikes Halt Flights at 13 Russian Airports, Hit Yaroslavl Refinery on Victory Day Eve

key_facts.fact: Air traffic at 13 airports across southern Russia was suspended after Ukrainian drones struck the regional air navigation center in Rostov-on-Don
key_facts.excerpt: Air traffic at 13 airports in southern Russia has been suspended after drones struck a building at a local air navigation center in Rostov-on-Don, the Russian transport ministry said. The strike led to the suspension of flights to and from airports in Astrakhan, Vladikavkaz, Volgograd, Gelendzhik, Grozny, Krasnodar, Makhachkala, Magas, Mineralnye Vody, Nalchik, Sochi, Stavropol and Elista.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine struck the Yaroslavl Oil Refinery, located about 700 kilometers from the Ukrainian border, causing a fire on site
key_facts.excerpt: In Russia's Yaroslavl region, Ukraine's Defense Forces struck the Yaroslavl Oil Refinery. A fire was reported on the facility's grounds. As Ukrinform previously reported, Ukraine's Defense Forces struck an oil industry facility in Yaroslavl, Russia, located about 700 kilometers from the Ukrainian border.

key_facts.fact: Russia's Defense Ministry said it downed 264 Ukrainian drones early Friday; Russia and Ukraine accused each other of breaching Moscow's unilateral May 8-10 Victory Day truce
key_facts.excerpt: The Kremlin said its forces downed 264 Ukrainian drones early on Friday, with officials in Moscow reporting attempted attacks on the capital and in the Perm region in the Ural Mountains. The truce, declared from May 8 to May 10, was intended to cover annual celebrations that include a military parade in Moscow.

key_facts.fact: President Zelenskyy described the deep strikes as 'long-range sanctions'; Ukraine has hit the Tuapse refinery four times in recent campaigns
key_facts.excerpt: Al Jazeera's Audrey McAlpine, reporting from Kyiv, said Ukraine has taken responsibility for the overnight strike on the oil refinery, with a new term being used by Ukrainian officials to describe such actions as 'long range sanctions'. The Tuapse oil refinery [Black sea coast] its been hit four times.

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian commander Syrskyi said Ukrainian drones carried out nearly 357,000 combat missions in April, striking more than 160,700 verified targets
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian drone systems carried out nearly 357,000 combat missions in April and struck more than 160,700 verified targets, 2% more than in March, according to Syrskyi.

key_facts.fact: Russia is deploying four additional anti-drone regiments, 24 battalions and 162 batteries, and reinforcing layered air defenses around Moscow and Krasnodar Krai
key_facts.excerpt: According to Syrskyi, Russia is deploying an additional four regiments, 24 battalions, and 162 batteries to counter Ukrainian strike drones while also strengthening layered air defense coverage around Moscow and Krasnodar Krai.

stories.headline: US Disables Two Iranian Tankers in Strait of Hormuz; Rubio Awaits Iran's Reply on 14-Point Peace Proposal

key_facts.fact: A US fighter jet disabled two Iranian-flagged tankers on Friday May 8, prompting retaliatory attacks and rattling the month-old ceasefire
key_facts.excerpt: A US fighter jet on Friday, May 8, disabled two Iranian-flagged tankers, prompting retaliatory attacks and rattling a shaky truce as President Donald Trump said he was awaiting Tehran's reply to his latest proposal to end the war.

key_facts.fact: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in Rome the US expects an Iranian response on the peace proposal Friday: 'We should know something today'
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the U.S. is expecting a response on Friday from Iran on the proposal to end the war. 'We should know something today. ... We're expecting a response from them,' Rubio told reporters in Rome on Friday.

key_facts.fact: The 14-point US proposal, delivered via Pakistani mediators, would require Iran to forgo nuclear weapons and halt uranium enrichment for at least 12 years and surrender about 440 kg of 60%-enriched uranium
key_facts.excerpt: According to US media reports, Washington sent Iran a 14-point document earlier this week. Under its proposals, Iran would be required to agree not to develop a nuclear weapon and halt all enrichment of uranium for at least 12 years. It would also be required to hand over an estimated 440kg (970lb) stock of uranium, which it has enriched to 60 percent.

key_facts.fact: US CENTCOM said it responded to attacks on three US Navy ships in the Strait of Hormuz with self-defense strikes — the first US airstrikes on Iranian soil since the month-old ceasefire
key_facts.excerpt: This is the first report of U.S. airstrikes on Iranian soil since the ceasefire a month ago. CENTCOM says it responded to, quote, 'unprovoked Iranian attacks' and responded with self-defense strikes yesterday after, they say, three U.S. Navy ships were attacked by Iranian speedboats, missiles and drones.

key_facts.fact: Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz since hostilities began Feb. 28; about 13 million barrels per day of oil are off the market
key_facts.excerpt: This waterway is vital to the world, but Iran has blocked access to it to ships since the start of the war. And, you know, with ships unable to transit, we're seeing really high oil prices because there's now 13 million barrels of oil a day off the market.

key_facts.fact: Iran's UN envoy Amir Saeed Irvani sent a letter to the UN secretary-general accusing the US of violating the ceasefire with the tanker strikes
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's UN envoy, Amir Saeed Irvani, accused the US of violating the ceasefire with the attacks on the Iranian tankers, in a letter to the UN secretary-general and Security Council.

stories.headline: Reform UK Surges in 2026 Local Elections, Seizing Labour Heartlands; Labour Faces Worst Result This Century

key_facts.fact: Reform UK gained 583 councillors and seized control of four councils in early returns; Labour shed 394 councillors and 11 councils
key_facts.excerpt: Labour has suffered the heaviest losses, shedding 394 councillors and 11 councils, while the Conservatives have also declined, losing 267 councillors and three councils. The standout story, however, is Reform UK's dramatic breakthrough. The party has gained 583 councillors — taking its total to 585 — and seized control of four councils, having held none previously.

key_facts.fact: Reform took all 14 seats Labour was defending in Tameside (Greater Manchester), and all 22 seats in Wigan, where the local MP is Cabinet minister Lisa Nandy
key_facts.excerpt: Take Tameside in Greater Manchester, the patch of the former deputy prime minister Angela Rayner. Labour was defending 17 seats and lost 16 of them, all to Reform. Not far away in Wigan, where the local MP is the cabinet minister Lisa Nandy, Labour lost all 22 seats it was defending to Reform.

key_facts.fact: Councils in Gateshead, Sunderland and Wakefield — under continuous Labour control since 1973 — fell to Reform; Sandwell, Labour-held since 1979, also flipped
key_facts.excerpt: Councils in Gateshead, Sunderland, and Wakefield, which had been under continuous Labour control since their formation in 1973, saw Reform win enough seats to take full control. Similarly, Sandwell, a Labour stronghold since 1979, saw Reform become the new majority party.

key_facts.fact: Welsh Labour leader and First Minister Eluned Morgan lost her seat as Labour faced near-wipeout in Wales, ending a winning streak of more than 100 years
key_facts.excerpt: Wales has been red for more than 100 years. Now Labour's on course for near wipeout there, as the left-wing Welsh nationalists in Plaid Cymru and Reform sweep the board. It was so bad in Wales that Eluned Morgan, the Labour leader there and the serving first minister, didn't even win her seat.

key_facts.fact: Hartlepool MP Jonathan Brash and other backbenchers called on Prime Minister Keir Starmer to step down following the results
key_facts.excerpt: Hartlepool's Labour MP Jonathan, a long-time critic of Sir Starmer, called for the Minister to step down the results.

key_facts.fact: Conservatives lost their majority in Hampshire for the first time since 1997, with Reform the main beneficiary; turnout reached 42%, up seven points from 2022
key_facts.excerpt: Hampshire witnessed a similar outcome, as the Conservatives lost their majority for the first time since 1997, again to Reform, though no single party secured overall control there. Turnout is proving to be notably higher than recent local elections. It is, so far, running at 42%, up seven points on 2022.

stories.headline: Honeywell-Backed Quantinuum Files for Nasdaq IPO Under 'QNT' Ticker

key_facts.fact: Quantinuum publicly filed Form S-1 with the SEC on May 8, 2026 for an IPO of Class A common stock to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under ticker 'QNT'
key_facts.excerpt: Honeywell (NASDAQ: HON) today announced that Quantinuum, a leading, full-stack quantum computing company, has publicly filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the 'SEC') relating to a proposed initial public offering of shares of its Class A common stock. Quantinuum intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol 'QNT.'

key_facts.fact: Quantinuum reported 2025 revenue of $30.9 million and a net loss of $192.6 million, vs $23.0 million revenue and $144.1 million loss in the prior year
key_facts.excerpt: In its filing, the company reported 2025 revenue of $30.9 million and a net loss of $192.6 million, versus $23.0 million of revenue and a $144.1 million loss the prior year.

key_facts.fact: The company has invested more than $2 billion in R&D over the past decade and last year raised about $600 million at a $10 billion pre-money valuation, including from Nvidia's venture arm
key_facts.excerpt: The firm has invested more than $2 billion in research and development over the last decade and is currently in the early stages of commercial growth. Quantinuum, which plans to sell new shares in the offering, last year raised about $600 million from investors including Nvidia's venture capital arm at a $10 billion pre-money valuation.

key_facts.fact: Quantinuum was formed in 2021 by combining Honeywell Quantum Solutions with Cambridge Quantum; J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley are joint lead bookrunners
key_facts.excerpt: Quantinuum was formed in 2021 by combining Honeywell's quantum computing division and Cambridge Quantum. J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley are the joint lead active book-running managers.

key_facts.fact: The number of shares and price range have not yet been set; Quantinuum is headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado, with facilities in the UK, Germany, Japan and Singapore
key_facts.excerpt: The IPO terms, including the number of shares and price range, have not yet been determined, and the offering remains subject to market conditions and SEC effectiveness requirements. Quantinuum's headquarters is in Broomfield, Colorado, with additional facilities across United Kingdom, Germany, Japan, and Singapore.

stories.headline: Alphabet's Isomorphic Labs in Talks to Raise Over $2B Led by Thrive Capital for AI Drug Discovery

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic Labs, the AI drug discovery company spun out of Google DeepMind, is in advanced talks to raise more than $2 billion, according to people familiar with the plan
key_facts.excerpt: Isomorphic Labs, an AI-powered drug discovery company spun out of Alphabet Inc.'s Google DeepMind, is in advanced discussions to raise more than $2 billion in a new round of funding, according to people familiar with the plan.

key_facts.fact: Thrive Capital, which led Isomorphic's first external round last year, is set to lead the new financing; Alphabet is also participating
key_facts.excerpt: Thrive Capital, the venture firm that led Isomorphic Labs' first funding round last year, is set to lead the new financing, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity as the information is not public. Alphabet is also participating, one person said, though the round is not yet closed.

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic raised $600 million in March 2025 in its first external round (also led by Thrive) and signed research collaborations with Eli Lilly and Novartis worth nearly $3 billion in potential milestone payments
key_facts.excerpt: In March 2025, Isomorphic raised $600 million in its first external funding round, led by Thrive Capital with participation from Alphabet and GV. It also signed major research collaborations with Eli Lilly and Novartis that carried potential milestone payments of nearly $3 billion combined.

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic plans to use the round to enhance its IsoDDE drug design engine and grow its international presence
key_facts.excerpt: Isomorphic Labs reportedly plans to use the funding round that it's raising to enhance IsoDDE. The Alphabet unit also plans to grow its international presence.

stories.headline: FDA Approves First Drug for NRG1-Fusion Bile Duct Cancer Under New National Priority Voucher Program

key_facts.fact: On May 8, 2026, the FDA approved zenocutuzumab-zbco (Bizengri, Partner Therapeutics) for adults with advanced, unresectable or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring an NRG1 gene fusion after prior systemic therapy
key_facts.excerpt: On May 8, 2026, the Food and Drug Administration approved zenocutuzumab-zbco (Bizengri, Partner Therapeutics, Inc.) for adults with advanced, unresectable or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring a neuregulin 1 (NRG1) gene fusion with disease progression on or after prior systemic therapy. NRG1-fusion positive cholangiocarcinoma is an extremely rare, life-threatening malignancy.

key_facts.fact: The approval is the seventh under the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program designed to expedite reviews for rare diseases
key_facts.excerpt: This approval marks the seventh approval under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program.

key_facts.fact: In the eNRGy trial, 19 evaluable patients with NRG1-fusion cholangiocarcinoma had a 36.8% confirmed overall response rate, with duration of response ranging from 2.8 to 12.9 months
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 22 patients with unresectable or metastatic NRG1 fusion-positive cholangiocarcinoma were enrolled in the eNRGy trial with 19 evaluable for efficacy. ORR was 36.8% (95% CI: 16.3, 61.6) and the DOR ranged from 2.8 to 12.9 months.

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved the application over five months ahead of its goal date; approval came just two days after Partner Therapeutics was granted the fast-track voucher
key_facts.excerpt: Approval comes just two days after the privately held company was granted the fast-track voucher for the drug.

key_facts.fact: Bizengri was already approved in 2024 for NRG1-fusion non-small cell lung cancer and pancreatic adenocarcinoma after prior therapy
key_facts.excerpt: In 2024, Bizengri received accelerated approval for the treatment of adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer and pancreatic adenocarcinoma harboring a NRG1 gene fusion with disease progression on or after prior systemic therapy.
